questions.topic: Operational responsibility during computer downtime
questions.trigger: A pharmacy manager is reviewing the pharmacy's computer-downtime procedure. Which processes must the written procedure address?
questions.legal_decision: Retain professional safeguards during system downtime.
questions.critical_exception: The procedure must address the listed processes, even if its particular implementation varies.
questions.counterfactual_flip: Restoring the system does not excuse reconciling downtime dispensing events.
questions.stem: A pharmacy manager is reviewing the pharmacy's computer-downtime procedure. Which processes must the written procedure address? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Processing prescriptions during system outages.
choices.why: Correct. The procedure must address filling prescriptions during downtime.

choices.text: Entering downtime dispensations into patient profiles after restoration.
choices.why: Correct. The procedure must ensure that computerized patient profiles are updated.

choices.text: Obtaining new prescriber signatures for previously valid prescriptions.
choices.why: Incorrect. The downtime provision does not impose this additional signature requirement.

choices.text: Conducting appropriate drug utilization review during downtime.
choices.why: Correct. DUR must be addressed despite loss of computer functionality.

choices.text: Maintaining continuity of care when needed.
choices.why: Correct. Continuity of care when necessary is expressly included.

questions.topic: New prescription pickup during sole-pharmacist break
questions.trigger: During a lawful on-premises break, a sole pharmacist leaves the prescription area. A patient arrives for a new prescription already prepared, visually checked and subjected to pharmacist drug utilization review. Which measures are required under the temporary-absence rule?
questions.legal_decision: Apply the specific new-prescription pickup pathway during a lawful break.
questions.critical_exception: Prior preparation, visual check and pharmacist DUR are stipulated; other security, premises and break conditions remain applicable.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If checking or DUR has not occurred, the new-prescription exception is unavailable.
questions.stem: During a lawful on-premises break, a sole pharmacist leaves the prescription area. A patient arrives for a new prescription already prepared, visually checked and subjected to pharmacist drug utilization review. Which measures are required under the temporary-absence rule? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Obtain the prescriber's confirmation of the completed prescription.
choices.why: Incorrect. Additional prescriber confirmation is not required by the break exception.

choices.text: Keep a transaction log that includes the patient's telephone number.
choices.why: Correct. The new-prescription pickup exception requires a log with the patient's telephone number.

choices.text: Have the pharmacist call the patient within a reasonable time after returning.
choices.why: Correct. The pharmacist must follow up within a reasonable time for pertinent counseling.

choices.text: Have the pharmacist review ancillary-staff duties performed during the absence.
choices.why: Correct. The rule requires review of support personnel's work upon return.

choices.text: Have a certified technician perform the follow-up counseling before release.
choices.why: Incorrect. Certification does not authorize actual patient counseling.

critical_error_options.reason: Delegates patient counseling to a technician.

questions.topic: Drug samples for retail inventory
questions.trigger: May a pharmacy accept manufacturer samples marked not for resale for subsequent commercial dispensing?
questions.legal_decision: Distinguish ordinary commercial inventory from not-for-resale samples.
questions.critical_exception: The question concerns resale, not a separately lawful no-charge sample program.
questions.counterfactual_flip: Lawfully acquired commercial stock is not subject to this sample-specific prohibition.
questions.stem: May a pharmacy accept manufacturer samples marked not for resale for subsequent commercial dispensing?

choices.text: Yes, provided the pharmacy charges only a dispensing fee.
choices.why: Incorrect. The proposed fee does not establish a lawful exception to the prohibition on resale.

choices.text: Yes, provided the pharmacy records the samples' lot numbers.
choices.why: Incorrect. Traceability does not change the restriction on resale.

choices.text: No; samples may not be accepted for the purpose of resale.
choices.why: Correct. Massachusetts prohibits accepting or purchasing such samples for compounding, repacking or resale.

choices.text: Yes, provided each supply is dispensed against a patient-specific prescription.
choices.why: Incorrect. A prescription does not authorize use of prohibited sample stock for resale.

choices.text: Yes, provided the manufacturer supplies written consent.
choices.why: Incorrect. Manufacturer consent does not waive the professional-practice rule.

questions.topic: Reinstatement after long disciplinary suspension

questions.legal_decision: Distinguish mandatory MPJE from possible NAPLEX for a long disciplinary suspension.
questions.critical_exception: Reinstatement also requires satisfaction of applicable Board orders and conditions.
questions.counterfactual_flip: An ordinary nondisciplinary lapse is evaluated under 4.02(5), rather than the long disciplinary-suspension provision.

choices.text: NAPLEX; the Board may waive MPJE.
choices.why: Incorrect. NAPLEX does not replace the required MPJE.

choices.text: Both NAPLEX and MPJE are mandatory in every case.
choices.why: Incorrect. The Board may require NAPLEX; it is not invariably mandatory.

choices.text: Only the MPJE may be required; the Board cannot require NAPLEX.
choices.why: Incorrect. The Board may impose NAPLEX as an additional condition.

choices.text: MPJE is mandatory; NAPLEX may also be required.
choices.why: Correct. A suspension exceeding two years requires MPJE and other Board conditions, which may include NAPLEX.

choices.text: Neither examination is required if missed CE is completed.
choices.why: Incorrect. CE completion does not replace the mandatory examination.

questions.topic: Continuing education across graduation and first full year
questions.trigger: A pharmacist graduated from a Board-approved pharmacy school and was licensed in 2025. The pharmacist works throughout 2026 in standard retail practice with no specialty CE obligations. What is the ordinary minimum CE total for 2026?

choices.text: 10 contact hours.
choices.why: Incorrect. The ordinary annual minimum is not ten hours in the year after graduation.

choices.text: 20 contact hours.
choices.why: Correct. The graduation-year exception applies to 2025; the 2026 minimum is 20 contact hours.

choices.text: 30 contact hours.
choices.why: Incorrect. Thirty is not the ordinary annual minimum.

choices.text: 40 contact hours.
choices.why: Incorrect. The ordinary two-year total does not remove the graduation-year exception.

choices.text: No contact hours.
choices.why: Incorrect. The graduation exception does not extend to the next calendar year.

questions.topic: Reporting final discipline in another profession versus pending charge
questions.trigger: A Massachusetts pharmacist also holds a nursing license in another state. The other state issues a final disciplinary order against the nursing license. questions.critical_exception: The facts stipulate a reportable charge, not a mere investigation.
questions.counterfactual_flip: Final action on another credential remains independently reportable absent a criminal charge.
questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist also holds a nursing license in another state. The other state issues a final disciplinary order against the nursing license. Separately, the pharmacist becomes subject to a reportable pending criminal charge. Which Massachusetts pharmacy reporting deadlines apply? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Report the final nursing order within 30 days.
choices.why: Incorrect. The final action on another health-care credential is subject to the seven-business-day provision.

choices.text: Report the pending charge within seven business days.
choices.why: Incorrect. Pending criminal charges are governed by the separate 30-day written-reporting provision.

choices.text: Report the final nursing-license action within seven business days.
choices.why: Correct. The rule reaches other health-care credentials and actions in other jurisdictions.

choices.text: Report the pending charge within 30 days only if a conviction follows.
choices.why: Incorrect. The rule covers a pending criminal charge independently of a conviction.

choices.text: Report the pending criminal charge in writing within 30 days.
choices.why: Correct. The criminal reporting provision requires a written report within 30 days.

questions.topic: Prescriber agent preparation versus signature responsibility
questions.trigger: An otherwise lawful paper prescription for a federally controlled medication is permitted in the circumstances. A prescriber's secretary types the drug, quantity and patient details. Who may sign the prescription as the issuing practitioner?
questions.legal_decision: Separate delegated preparation from practitioner issuance and signature.
questions.critical_exception: Paper issuance is stipulated to be permitted; all other applicable form requirements remain.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the issuing practitioner signs the appropriately prepared paper prescription, agent preparation alone is not a defect.
questions.stem: An otherwise lawful paper prescription for a federally controlled medication is permitted in the circumstances. A prescriber's secretary types the drug, quantity and patient details. Who may sign the prescription as the issuing practitioner?

choices.text: The prescribing practitioner, who remains responsible for its compliance.
choices.why: Correct. An agent may prepare the prescription, but practitioner signature and responsibility remain required.

choices.text: The secretary, if the practitioner subsequently reviews the prescription.
choices.why: Incorrect. Subsequent review cannot substitute for the required practitioner signature.

choices.text: The secretary, using the practitioner's signature stamp with permission.
choices.why: Incorrect. An agent's stamp is not the required manual practitioner signature.

choices.text: A pharmacist, after confirming the intended order with the secretary.
choices.why: Incorrect. The pharmacist cannot supply the practitioner's signature.

choices.text: Another practitioner who witnesses preparation but does not issue the order.
choices.why: Incorrect. Witnessing preparation does not make that practitioner the issuer.

critical_error_options.reason: Treats an agent signature as practitioner signature.
Treats delegated stamping as required manual signature.

questions.topic: Medical need notation for GHB
questions.trigger: What additional information must a practitioner note on a prescription for gamma-hydroxybutyric acid under federal law?
questions.legal_decision: Recognize a drug-specific federal prescription notation.
questions.critical_exception: The item tests prescription notation, not separate REMS distribution controls.
questions.counterfactual_flip: For another drug, its applicable prescription-content and distribution requirements govern.
questions.stem: What additional information must a practitioner note on a prescription for gamma-hydroxybutyric acid under federal law?

choices.text: The patient's insurer's prior-authorization number.
choices.why: Incorrect. Insurance authorization is not the special prescription notation.

choices.text: The dispensing pharmacy's DEA registration number.
choices.why: Incorrect. The pharmacy's registration is not the required special entry.

choices.text: The prescriber's specialty certification number.
choices.why: Incorrect. Specialty certification is not the specified notation.

choices.text: The patient's prior controlled-substance refill dates.
choices.why: Incorrect. Refill dates are not the required special entry.

choices.text: The patient's medical need for the prescription.
choices.why: Correct. The federal prescription-issuance regulation expressly requires this notation.

questions.topic: Missing versus incorrect patient address on Schedule II order
questions.trigger: A permitted, otherwise valid new paper Schedule II prescription omits the patient's address. The pharmacist independently verifies the address. What does Massachusetts prescription-change policy allow?
questions.legal_decision: Distinguish addition of an omitted address from changing an existing one.
questions.critical_exception: The address has been verified; no change of patient identity is contemplated.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the existing address is incorrect, the state policy requires consultation with the prescriber or authorized agent before changing it.
questions.stem: A permitted, otherwise valid new paper Schedule II prescription omits the patient's address. The pharmacist independently verifies the address. What does Massachusetts prescription-change policy allow?

choices.text: Obtain a replacement prescription because the address is omitted.
choices.why: Incorrect. The policy allows addition of an omitted patient address.

choices.text: Add the verified address without consulting the prescriber.
choices.why: Correct. An omitted patient address may be added without consultation.

choices.text: Consult the prescriber before adding the address.
choices.why: Incorrect. Consultation is required for changing an existing patient address, not for adding an omitted one.

choices.text: Have the patient's agent sign the prescriber's portion of the prescription.
choices.why: Incorrect. The patient's agent cannot supply the practitioner's signature.

choices.text: Process the prescription without adding the address.
choices.why: Incorrect. The address is required information; the permitted addition resolves the omission.

questions.topic: Non-OTP emergency direct dispensing versus prescription issuance
questions.trigger: A DEA-registered practitioner not separately registered as an opioid treatment program is arranging referral for a patient requiring urgent initiation of narcotic dependence treatment. questions.counterfactual_flip: An authorized OTP uses its own applicable treatment requirements.

Assume state and local law permit the direct dispensing described. Which statements reflect the federal emergency provision? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

questions.topic: Emergency naloxone administration by pharmacy licensees

questions.legal_decision: Distinguish emergency opioid-antagonist administration from ordinary prescribing.

questions.stem: A visitor appears to be experiencing an opioid-related overdose in a Massachusetts retail pharmacy. The pharmacist is calling for emergency assistance. choices.text: Emergency administration is restricted to pharmacists.

choices.text: A pharmacy licensee may administer naloxone to a person appearing to have an opioid-related overdose.

choices.why: Incorrect. The emergency overdose provision does not require a new patient-specific prescription.

choices.why: Incorrect. Rescue administration does not confer independent prescribing authority.

questions.topic: Recording a declined counseling offer

choices.text: The patient profile, signature log or another suitable record system.

choices.text: Only the original written prescription.
choices.why: Incorrect. The statute does not require that exclusive location.

choices.text: Only the computerized medication profile.
choices.why: Incorrect. Manual profiles and other systems are also permitted.

choices.why: Incorrect. The statute does not prescribe a separate form.

questions.topic: Repeated therapy and offer to counsel
questions.trigger: A patient obtains a routine refill of long-established therapy. The pharmacist identifies no significant health or safety issue requiring actual counseling. The patient has not yet been offered counseling today. What is the proper action?
questions.legal_decision: Distinguish the general counseling offer from required proactive counseling.
questions.critical_exception: No new or significant therapy is stated; acceptance calls for the counseling service.
questions.counterfactual_flip: A new therapy or significant health/safety concern would require appropriate counseling unless declined.
questions.stem: A patient obtains a routine refill of long-established therapy. The pharmacist identifies no significant health or safety issue requiring actual counseling. The patient has not yet been offered counseling today. What is the proper action?

choices.text: Provide a complete new-therapy counseling session before each refill.
choices.why: Incorrect. Actual counseling is required for new and significant therapies; the offer is broader.

choices.text: Omit the offer because the medication is a refill.
choices.why: Incorrect. The offer applies to each recipient.

choices.why: Correct. Routine refill status does not eliminate the offer.

choices.text: Have a trained technician provide actual clinical counseling if requested.
choices.why: Incorrect. Technicians may offer, but not perform, actual counseling.

choices.text: Treat acceptance on the prior refill as refusal of today's offer.
choices.why: Incorrect. A prior counseling encounter does not establish a current refusal.

questions.topic: Properly dispensed nondefective medication returned by patient

questions.counterfactual_flip: An error or suspected defect would trigger mandatory acceptance, quarantine and appropriate disposition.

questions.topic: Single non-child-resistant OTC package size

It wants to supply a conventional package size for consumers unable to open the child-resistant package. The ordinary warning fits on the principal display panel. Which arrangement meets the specific exception?
questions.legal_decision: Recognize the manufacturer's limited noncomplying package-size exception.
questions.critical_exception: A too-small display panel may qualify for a substitute warning, but that condition is excluded.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If complying packaging is not also supplied, this single-size exception is unavailable.
questions.stem: A manufacturer markets an OTC product subject to federal special-packaging requirements. It wants to supply a conventional package size for consumers unable to open the child-resistant package. The ordinary warning fits on the principal display panel. Which arrangement meets the specific exception?

choices.text: Market all sizes conventionally with a warning on the back panel.
choices.why: Incorrect. The exception is limited to one noncomplying size with conspicuous principal-display labeling.

choices.text: Market a single conventional size and discontinue complying sizes.
choices.why: Incorrect. Complying packaging must also be supplied.

choices.text: Supply complying packaging and one conventional size with the required conspicuous warning.
choices.why: Correct. This meets the single-size alternative and labeling conditions.

choices.text: Supply conventional packaging to consumers over age 65 without the warning.
choices.why: Incorrect. Purchaser age does not substitute for the warning.

choices.text: Use an individual pharmacy patient's request as authority for the manufacturer's entire product line.
choices.why: Incorrect. Prescription packaging waiver and the manufacturer's exception are distinct.

questions.topic: Pseudoephedrine seller training covers cashier
questions.trigger: A pharmacy sells pseudoephedrine at a restricted counter. One employee hands the product to customers, and another directly accepts payment. Which federal seller-training obligations apply?
questions.legal_decision: Identify covered sales roles and associated documentation.
questions.critical_exception: Placement, purchaser identification and sales-log requirements apply separately.
questions.counterfactual_flip: An employee with neither covered sales role is not covered by this particular description merely by working in the store.
questions.stem: A pharmacy sells pseudoephedrine at a restricted counter. One employee hands the product to customers, and another directly accepts payment. Which federal seller-training obligations apply? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Train the employee handing the product to purchasers.
choices.why: Correct. Employees responsible for delivering product into purchasers' custody are covered.

choices.text: Exclude the cashier because the cashier does not handle the product.
choices.why: Incorrect. Employees dealing directly with purchasers by obtaining payment are also covered.

choices.text: Train the employee directly accepting payment for these products.
choices.why: Correct. The payment-taking employee falls within the regulated seller's obligation.

choices.text: Maintain self-certification and records demonstrating covered employees' training.
choices.why: Correct. The regulation requires retention of the self-certification and training evidence.

choices.text: Substitute state pharmacist licensure for the seller's federal self-certification.
choices.why: Incorrect. State professional licensure does not replace applicable seller self-certification.

questions.topic: Purchaser cancellation of paper DEA Form 222
questions.trigger: A purchaser wishes to cancel an unshipped item on a paper DEA Form 222. What is the applicable procedure?
questions.legal_decision: Distinguish purchaser cancellation from supplier voiding and lost-form reporting.
questions.critical_exception: The unshipped item and original order documentation are the relevant facts.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the supplier initiates voiding, it notifies the purchaser in writing and records the voiding.
questions.stem: A purchaser wishes to cancel an unshipped item on a paper DEA Form 222. What is the applicable procedure?

choices.text: Erase the item on the purchaser's retained copy and notify the supplier orally.
choices.why: Incorrect. The purchaser must notify the supplier in writing; changing its own copy alone is insufficient.

choices.text: Issue a replacement Form 222 as the required method of cancellation.
choices.why: Incorrect. Written notice is the specified cancellation procedure, not necessarily a new form.

choices.text: Request DEA to invalidate the supplier's original form.
choices.why: Incorrect. Ordinary cancellation is handled directly with the supplier.

choices.text: Have the supplier return the original for the purchaser to overwrite.
choices.why: Incorrect. The supplier must document cancellation on the original form.

choices.text: Notify the supplier in writing; the supplier records cancellation on the original.
choices.why: Correct. This follows the purchaser cancellation procedure.

questions.topic: Refrigerated medication storage and excursion records
questions.trigger: A Massachusetts pharmacy is replacing its medication refrigerator and updating temperature logs. Which requirements are expressly imposed by the storage regulation?
questions.legal_decision: Apply equipment and record requirements for refrigerated medications.
questions.critical_exception: Appropriate units and any applicable Board-approved equipment exceptions must be evaluated.
questions.counterfactual_flip: After an excursion, assess integrity under the procedure rather than assuming product suitability.
questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is replacing its medication refrigerator and updating temperature logs. Which requirements are expressly imposed by the storage regulation? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: A calibrated dorm-style refrigerator with an internal freezer compartment is acceptable.
choices.why: Incorrect. The regulation prohibits a refrigerator with a freezer compartment inside it.

choices.text: Include a protocol for assessing medication integrity after out-of-range temperatures.
choices.why: Correct. The procedure must address excursions and product integrity.

choices.text: Keep temperature logs and documented responses for at least one year.
choices.why: Correct. The regulation establishes this retention period.

choices.text: Keep food and beverages out of refrigerators and freezers used for medication.
choices.why: Correct. Storage of food or beverages in medication units is prohibited.

choices.text: Replace temperature logs with an equipment warranty and calibration certificate.
choices.why: Incorrect. Neither documents actual temperatures and corrective action.

questions.topic: Retention of pharmacy self-inspection tool
questions.trigger: For how long must a Massachusetts pharmacy retain its completed Board-approved self-inspection tool?
questions.legal_decision: Distinguish record retention from frequency of inspection.
questions.critical_exception: Self-inspection is separately required at least annually and following specified events.
questions.counterfactual_flip: A temperature log has a different one-year minimum under 9.22(4).
questions.stem: For how long must a Massachusetts pharmacy retain its completed Board-approved self-inspection tool?

choices.text: At least two years.
choices.why: Correct. The pharmacy operation regulation establishes a two-year retention period.

choices.text: At least one year.
choices.why: Incorrect. One year is the minimum for specified temperature records, not this tool.

choices.text: At least three years.
choices.why: Incorrect. Three years is not the specified minimum.

choices.text: At least five years.
choices.why: Incorrect. Five years is not the specified minimum.

choices.text: Until the next self-inspection.
choices.why: Incorrect. The next inspection does not eliminate the retention requirement.

questions.topic: Interstate direct delivery to qualifying LTCF
questions.trigger: A Massachusetts retail pharmacy proposes delivering prescribed Schedule II narcotic medication to a patient admitted to a Maine long-term care facility. The prescription and applicable state and DEA registration requirements are satisfied. Which method does the specific Massachusetts LTCF delivery exception permit?
questions.legal_decision: Recognize the specific direct LTCF courier exception.
questions.critical_exception: Maine or a contiguous state, facility admission, licensure and registration are material facts.
questions.counterfactual_flip: Ordinary interstate home delivery is evaluated under separate address and carrier conditions.
questions.stem: A Massachusetts retail pharmacy proposes delivering prescribed Schedule II narcotic medication to a patient admitted to a Maine long-term care facility. The prescription and applicable state and DEA registration requirements are satisfied. Which method does the specific Massachusetts LTCF delivery exception permit?

choices.text: Delivery to a Massachusetts retail pickup location for forwarding.
choices.why: Incorrect. The exception specifies direct delivery to the qualifying facility.

choices.text: Delivery to a facility employee's private residence for later transport.
choices.why: Incorrect. That does not meet the direct-to-facility requirement.

choices.text: Only postal delivery to the patient's former home address.
choices.why: Incorrect. Direct courier delivery to the facility is specifically permitted.

choices.text: Direct delivery to the facility by a pharmacy-employed or contracted courier.
choices.why: Correct. The statutory exception expressly authorizes this method.

choices.text: Delivery by any method once the patient signs a waiver.
choices.why: Incorrect. Consent does not replace statutory delivery conditions.

questions.topic: Abuse-deterrent interchange priority over cheaper conventional product
questions.trigger: A Massachusetts Drug Store pharmacy receives a prescription for a drug the state Drug Formulary Commission has identified as posing heightened abuse risk. No no-substitution instruction appears. A designated interchangeable abuse-deterrent alternative and a cheaper ordinary interchangeable product are available. Other requirements are met. What is the statutory selection priority?
questions.legal_decision: Apply the designated abuse-deterrent priority before ordinary price-based interchange.
questions.critical_exception: Actual state-designated interchangeability, availability and no no-substitution direction are stipulated.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If no designated interchangeable abuse-deterrent product exists, the ordinary less-expensive reasonably available interchange rule applies.
questions.stem: A Massachusetts Drug Store pharmacy receives a prescription for a drug the state Drug Formulary Commission has identified as posing heightened abuse risk. No no-substitution instruction appears. A designated interchangeable abuse-deterrent alternative and a cheaper ordinary interchangeable product are available. Other requirements are met. What is the statutory selection priority?

choices.text: Dispense the cheaper ordinary interchangeable product because price controls selection.
choices.why: Incorrect. The statute prioritizes an available designated interchangeable abuse-deterrent product.

choices.text: Dispense the designated interchangeable abuse-deterrent product.
choices.why: Correct. The statute prioritizes this product, then the eligible lower-cost alternative if none exists.

choices.text: Dispense the prescribed product because opioid interchange requires a new order.
choices.why: Incorrect. No separate prohibition or no-substitution instruction is asserted.

choices.text: Let the insurer's preference determine the statutory interchange obligation.
choices.why: Incorrect. Coverage preferences do not substitute for state product-selection requirements.

choices.text: Choose any product the manufacturer describes as abuse-deterrent.
choices.why: Incorrect. The rule concerns specifically identified interchangeable abuse-deterrent products.

questions.citation: M.G.L. c.112 §12D, definitions and substitution paragraph

questions.topic: Nonviable particle excursion versus viable remediation
questions.trigger: A sterile compounding pharmacy detects action-level nonviable particle counts in an ISO 7 buffer room. Microbiology results do not show viable action-level growth. The Board has issued no special direction. Which actions are required under the September 2026 environmental monitoring policy?
questions.legal_decision: Separate nonviable suspension from the limited viable-result pathway.
questions.critical_exception: No different Board direction is asserted.
questions.counterfactual_flip: For certain viable action-level buffer-room findings, the risk assessment and restricted BUD pathway may be available if its conditions are met.
questions.stem: A sterile compounding pharmacy detects action-level nonviable particle counts in an ISO 7 buffer room. Microbiology results do not show viable action-level growth. The Board has issued no special direction. Which actions are required under the September 2026 environmental monitoring policy? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Suspend compounding until full remediation and recertification of all ISO-classified areas.
choices.why: Correct. Nonviable action-level findings require suspension and full remediation/recertification absent different Board direction.

choices.text: Investigate the cause and implement corrective action.
choices.why: Correct. Action-level environmental findings require investigation and remediation.

choices.text: Resume with a 24-hour room-temperature BUD as soon as cleaning begins.
choices.why: Incorrect. Shortened-BUD pathways apply to specified viable action-level findings, not this nonviable excursion.

choices.text: Activate the continuity-of-care plan during suspension.
choices.why: Correct. A pharmacy suspending sterile compounding must implement the plan to meet patient needs.

choices.text: Maintain the relevant remediation records for Board inspection.
choices.why: Correct. Environmental monitoring and remediation records must be maintained and available.

critical_error_options.reason: Applies viable-result exception to nonviable excursion.

questions.topic: Pharmacy operating-name notification
questions.trigger: A licensed Massachusetts pharmacy changes its operating name without a change of ownership, location or configuration. Corporate paperwork authorizes the new name. What is required?
questions.legal_decision: Separate name-change notification from ownership or relocation procedures.
questions.critical_exception: No ownership, location or configuration change is asserted.
questions.counterfactual_flip: Ownership transfer or relocation invokes its own procedures.
questions.stem: A licensed Massachusetts pharmacy changes its operating name without a change of ownership, location or configuration. Corporate paperwork authorizes the new name. What is required?

choices.text: Notify the Board within seven days of the change.
choices.why: Incorrect. The operating-name notification period is 14 days.

choices.text: Notify the Board at the next license renewal.
choices.why: Incorrect. There is a separate prompt notice requirement.

choices.text: Notify the Board in writing within 14 days and include authorizing documentation.
choices.why: Correct. This meets the operating-name notification requirements.

choices.text: Apply for a relocation license because the name changed.
choices.why: Incorrect. No relocation is described.

choices.text: Notify the Board within 30 days by telephone.
choices.why: Incorrect. Written notice with documentation within 14 days is required.
